property_summary: For any depositor and any log-address, a successful Deposit call on the correct contract always increases the depositor's balances mapping by the msg.value (i.e., balances(addr) after Deposit equals previous + value) whereas the mutated contract can revert or leave balances unchanged if the external Log.AddMessage reverts or triggers reentrancy before balances update.

For any depositor and any log contract address, a successful Deposit call on the correct contract always increases balances(depositor) by the deposited msg.value (i.e., balances after == balances before + value); the mutant that calls Log.AddMessage before updating balances can leave balances unchanged (or revert) when the log call reverts or re-enters, so this rule can be violated for some inputs when the log misbehaves.

For any depositor and any non-reverting Log contract, a successful Deposit call on the reference C always increases balances(depositor) by msg.value (balances_after == balances_before + value); if the Log call can revert (or cause reentrancy), the mutant that logs before updating balances can cause Deposit to revert or leave balances unchanged, violating this property for some inputs.

For any depositor D and any amount v>0 when the log contract's AddMessage reverts, the reference C's Deposit will revert only after balances is unchanged (i.e., balances(D) does not increase on failed log), but more usefully: if the log contract's AddMessage REVERTS, the reference C's balances remain unchanged and the call reverts — the mutant that logs before updating balances may either revert (keeping balances unchanged) or, if the log is malicious and re-enters, can cause balances to increase at an unexpected key due to reentrancy; we capture this by asserting that when Deposit returns successfully then balances(depositor) == old + v for all inputs with a well-behaved log, and we create a malicious reentrant Log to cause the mutant to break this rule for some fuzzed params.

For any depositor and any deposit value, if Deposit returns successfully then the depositor's balance increases by exactly msg.value on the reference implementation; a malicious Log that re-enters during logging can break this when the log is called before balances are updated (mutant).

Reference contract never lets a Deposit call cause balances[anyAddress] to wrap below its previous value (i.e. balances[key] after Deposit is >= previous balances[key]); removing the overflow check can make balances wrap and become smaller for some inputs.

For any caller and key, after Deposit the reference contract guarantees balances(key) is at least its previous value (no wraparound); removing the overflow check allows balances(key) to wrap and become smaller for some inputs.

For any caller and any recipient key, a Deposit made by caller cannot DECREASE any stored balances[key] in the correct contract (balances[key]_after >= balances[key]_before); the mutant that removed the overflow check allows arithmetic wrap so some Deposit can make balances[key] strictly smaller.

For any depositor and any key, performing Deposit never decreases that key's stored balance in the correct contract (balances[key]_after >= balances[key]_before); removing the overflow check allows overflow wrap so some Deposit can make a balance for some key strictly smaller.

For any caller and any amount, calling Deposit on the reference C never decreases the caller's own balance (balances[msg.sender] after >= before); removing the overflow check allows arithmetic wrap so some Deposit amounts can make the caller's balance strictly smaller.
